stories.title: RBI may raise repo rate to 6.25% by mid‑2027, Deutsche Bank says
stories.summary: Deutsche Bank expects the Reserve Bank of India to lift its policy repo rate to 6.25% by mid‑2027 as inflation stays high and growth remains robust. The bank projects CPI inflation around 6% in late 2026, easing to 4.7% by FY28, and GDP growth above 7% for FY27 and FY28.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: Ceasefire extended to wider Kherson region to aid Oleshky
stories.summary: A ceasefire that started early on Tuesday to allow food and medicine into the Russian‑occupied city of Oleshky has been broadened to cover the broader southern Kherson region. Several thousand residents of Oleshky remain without electricity, food or water, and all road routes out are considered unsafe. No reported violations of the truce have occurred since it began.

stories.title: Western nations warn of worsening food security in Sudan amid civil war
stories.summary: The war in Sudan has created a severe humanitarian crisis, with the World Health Organization reporting more than 33 million people need assistance. The United States and 30 other Western states issued a joint statement warning of an “alarming deterioration” in Sudan’s food security and urging the warring parties to remove obstacles to aid to prevent famine. Yusuf Roble of Islamic Relief said people returning to Omdurman found homes destroyed or looted and had very little to survive on.

stories.title: General Compute raises $100 million Series A and secures $400 million chip deal
stories.summary: General Compute announced a $100 million Series A round led by Blackbird Ventures and Abstract Ventures, valuing the startup at $800 million post‑money after a $60 million seed round in May. The round follows a $400 million agreement to purchase inference chips from SambaNova and the addition of Positron and Cerebras to its supplier portfolio, alongside a $100 million annual recurring revenue contract with a large customer.
stories.why: The capital backs General Compute’s strategy of using inference‑optimized chips and smaller, distributed data‑center sites, providing a differentiated alternative to GPU‑focused cloud providers.

stories.title: Coca-Cola raises profit forecast as premium drinks, sodas hold strong
stories.summary: Coca-Cola has lifted its annual profit forecast, driven by robust demand for a range of beverages, particularly zero-sugar options. stories.title: Google’s Genie 4 world model adds audio, more realistic worlds, and real-time steering
stories.summary: Google DeepMind released its newest world model, Genie 4, in research preview on Tuesday. The release of Genie 4 comes a couple of months after AI video startup Runway released its second world model, GWM Worlds 2 , a playable model that responds dynamically to user inputs and includes audio generation.

stories.previousTitle: Google DeepMind releases Genie 4 world model in research preview
stories.previousSummary: Google DeepMind released Genie 4 as a research preview on Tuesday. It generates photorealistic, interactive worlds and adds real-time audio matching the environment, including music and dialogue. Users can edit scenes on the fly—changing weather, camera angle, or adding objects—and the system maintains a consistent simulation for up to two minutes, double its predecessor's limit. Gemini acts as director coordinating visuals while Genie generates them.

stories.title: RCMP probes Alberta health procurement for possible fraud, breach of trust and money laundering
stories.summary: Court documents filed this month in a wrongful‑dismissal lawsuit by former Alberta Health Services head Athana Mentzelopoulos state that the RCMP is investigating potential fraud, breach of trust and money‑laundering in provincial health‑care procurement contracts. The RCMP confirmed last year it was examining health‑care procurement but did not disclose details. Mentzelopoulos alleges she was dismissed for exposing “sweetheart” deals, while the government says she was fired for poor performance.
